sentences.text: However, during hearing on 05.12.2024, the parties were directed to seek the instructions in the matter.

3) Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that as per order dated 04.04.2022 in the proceedings of this case, Rs.5,00,000/- was directed to be deposited which is lying in the Fixed Deposit with the Registry of this Court.
As per office report dated 11.12.2024, the said amount with interest is now Rs.5,75,990/-.

4) He further submits that as per the instructions received, to put a quietus to this litigation, the petitioner is ready to pay respondent No.2 a further sum of Rs.2,25,000/- in addition to the amount deposited in the Fixed Deposit with accrued interest, making a total of Rs.8,00,000/-, in lieu of accusation of transaction of Rs.5,00,000/-.
5) Learned counsel for respondent No.2, on instructions, submits that if the petitioner pays the said amount, he is having no objection to quash the FIR registered against her.

6) Considering the aforesaid, as undertaken, the petitioner shall transfer the sum of Rs.2,25,000/-(Rupees Two Lakhs Twenty Five Thousand only) within a period of two weeks in the bank account of respondent No.2 by way of NEFT/RTGS.
7) Further, the amount which is lying in the Fixed Deposit be also transferred in the bank account of respondent No.2 by the Registry.
8) Learned counsel shall furnish the details of the bank account of respondent No.2 to the petitioner as well as to the Registry.
9) List the matter for final disposal on 03 rd January, 2025.

(NIDHI AHUJA) (NAND KISHOR)
 AR-cum-PS COURT MASTER (NSH)
